title: China's Only Silk-Sewn Jade Suit: 2,291 Plaques | Buried Empire P1 · 丝缕玉衣
description:
China's only jade burial suit sewn with silk — not gold — and the thread is still red after 2,000 years.

Unearthed in 1983 from the tomb of Zhao Mo, the second king of Nanyue (in today's Guangzhou), this suit is 2,291 hand-drilled jade plaques laced together with red silk thread. Every other jade suit ever found in China used gold, silver, or copper wire — this is the only silk-corded one known anywhere. Its front-opening jacket makes it unlike the royal suits of the north.

🧭 Expert Tip: See it at the Museum of the Mausoleum of the Nanyue King (南越王博物院) in Guangzhou — the tomb is preserved in situ beneath the galleries, so you walk the actual 2,000-year-old chambers. Go midweek mornings; it's near-empty.

2291块玉、一根红丝线——全世界唯一的丝缕玉衣，就在广州地下。
